b: ^The merchant turns a cracked cup in his hands. "You told me the spring has fallen silent. I should stop promising thirsty travelers a drink."
^The merchant shades his stall with a woven cloth. "A little honest work leaves the evening free for wonders."
^"You found the side passage yourself? Then you know more than the men who sell directions to it."
^"They say a narrow passage beyond the workshop leads to a spring that sings after sunset. I heard it from a boatman; I have never tasted its water."

c-1: ^"The courier needs provisions. Bring the agreed goods before the deadline; the payment is set aside."
c-2: ^"Find the courier during working hours. The workshop bench is yours to use, but a deadline waits for no oven."
c-3: ^"The courier spoke well of you. Reliable hands are worth more than loud promises."
c-5: ^"Dust in the channel, you say? Then I owe that boatman a question. I will tell travelers to carry their own water. Thank you for checking instead of repeating me."
